atomicity.reason: One obligation: publish the 30 % fallback limit while a raised request stays unconfirmed beyond 2 s; cooling and heating requests share the same rule and the 30 % definition is part of it.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: the fallback limit is defined inline (30 % of the full permitted discharge power) and the trigger and 2 s timeout are stated; the cooling and heating requests are the BMS's own requests.

feasibility.reason: A per-request acknowledgement timer and a capped power value are routine; the acknowledged-but-no-flow residual is documented in the linked risk and lies outside this requirement's claim.

parent_fit.reason: Implements the parent's observable: when the cooling and heating system stops responding the pack falls back to a reduced drive power because it can no longer keep its own temperature in check.

unambiguity.reason: Trigger, timeout and value are clear, but the limit is stated unconditionally while REQ_POWER_DERATING states a temperature-dependent value for the same output, so with both active (56 °C and an unconfirmed request: 30 % vs ramp 80 %; 59.5 °C: 30 % vs ramp 10 %) the requirements alone do not say which is published (the architecture takes the minimum).
unambiguity.suggestion: State the combination rule in the requirement ('the lower of the derating value and the fallback limit') and, optionally, say that 'confirmed' means receipt of the matching acknowledgement.

verifiability.reason: Concrete: raise a request, withhold the actuator's confirmation and check the published limit equals 30 % of the full permitted discharge power once 2 s have elapsed; a timely confirmation must not trigger it.

summary: Precise, testable fail-safe tied to the story and RISK_COOLANT_LOSS; unambiguity reduced because its combination with the derating ramp is unstated.
